sections.title: 1. Why Study Electronics and Communication Engineering in Ireland?

items: Ireland is a good destination for students interested in electronics, telecommunications, wireless communication and digital technologies. Its engineering programmes open doors to careers in fields like semiconductor manufacturing, medical devices, communications technology and electronic systems.
Key advantages of studying ECE in Ireland:
Technology industry exposure:
Exposure to career opportunities in the electronics, telecommunications, semiconductor technology and embedded systems industry.
Hands-on experience:
Gain expertise through electronic circuit laboratories, design projects and technical assignments.
Modern type specialisations: Like wireless networks, signal processing, microelectronics and Internet of Things (IoT) systems*.
Professional accreditation: A suitably accredited engineering degree* can aid your professional development.
Further education: Take master's programmes* in telecommunications, electronic engineering, computer engineering or related fields.
With Edu Hawk worldwide study abroad guidancestudents can check out these options and learn about the requirements needed to study abroad.

sections.title: 2. Electronics and Communication Engineering Courses in Ireland

items: Irish universities may not be called “Electronics and Communication Engineering”. Similar programs are often named Electrical and Electronic Engineering or Electronic and Computer Engineering.
Undergraduate courses
Bachelor of Engineering (BEng):* Length of time varies depending on qualification and university.
Bachelor of Engineering (Honours):* Usually a four year engineering degree.
Integrated Master of Engineering (MEng):* This is usually a five-year program and includes advanced engineering studies
Common Topics
ECE-related programs may consist of:
- Design of electronic circuits
*Digital logic & microprocessors
- Electronics - Digital & Analog
- Signals & Systems
- Processing of digital signals
- Communication systems
- Mobile and Wireless Communications
- Basics of radio frequency and antennas
- Microcontrollers & Embedded Systems
- Networks of computers
*Devices semiconductors
- Programming and Engineer’s Mathematics

sections.title: 4. Qualifications for study Electronics and Communication Engineering Course in Ireland

items: The eligibility criteria to study Electronics and Communication Engineering in Ireland differs from one university to another, the level of qualification, and the applicant’s educational background.
Eligibility for Undergraduate
Students applying after Class 12 are usually required to:
A recognized secondary school qualification.
Mathematics* with excellent academic performance.
Physics or other science subjects where required.
Grades which meet the entry criteria of the university.
Proof of proficiency in English*, if required.

Indian applicants should check the evaluation of their Class 12 board, grades and subject combination. Some students may require a foundation programme or other recognized qualification prior to an engineering degree.

sections.title: 5. Electronics and Communication Engineering Admission Requirements in Ireland

items: International applicants should check the specific admission requirements for Electronics and Communication Engineering in Ireland on a program by program basis.
Academic requirements

Universities look at academic grades, subject requirements and whether qualifications are equivalent. Mathematics is particularly important for engineering and Physics may be needed for undergraduate admission.
Requirements in English

They may need to sit IELTS Academic, TOEFL iBT, PTE Academic or an alternative English language test that is accepted. Minimum scores vary by institution and program. Some universities accept other evidence of English language ability
Additional requirements
Depending on the course applicants may need:
Certificates and Academic Records*
A statement of purpose or personal statement
Reference letters*
CV or resume for postgraduate admission
Evidence of relevant projects or work experience, if required
Proof of application fee* (if applicable)
Before you apply, make sure you check the most recent admissions guidance on the official university website.

sections.title: 7. Admission Procedure for Electronics and Communication Engineering in Ireland

items: 01. Step 01: The Electronics and Communication Engineering admission process in Ireland generally consists of the following steps.
02. Step 1: Choose a program.Electronic engineering and communications courses can be compared by modules, duration, accreditation, fees and placement opportunities.
03. Step 2: Confirm your eligibility. Check academic requirements, English language standards, and recognized international qualifications.
04. Step 3: Get the paperwork ready. Collect your passport, academic transcripts, certificates, English language results and any required statements or references
05. Step 4: Apply through the right channel. Most non-EU applicants apply directly through the university’s online application portal. The path depends on the institution and the type of applicant.
06. Step 5: Watch your application. Follow up on updates and provide any additional documents requested by the admissions team.
07. Step 6: Accept your offer Check terms, deposit, payment deadlines and fee conditions before confirming your place.
08. Step 7: Prepare to travel. If you need a student visa for Ireland
Accreditation is an important factor when selecting an engineering degree.
Engineers Ireland assesses engineering programs against educational and professional standards.
An accredited engineering qualification may assist with professional development and progression to professional engineering status, subject to the relevant requirements.
Check Before You Sign Up:
If the specific program is accredited.
Level of qualification the accreditation represents.
If accreditation applies to the year you plan to graduate.
The programme’s subject focus aligns with your future career goals

sections.title: 9. Salary and Career Opportunities for Electronics and Communication Engineers in Ireland

items: ECE graduates in Ireland can pursue technical jobs in electronics, telecom, computer hardware and connected systems.
Popular career paths
- Electronic Design Engineer
Telecom Engineer
- Engineer, Embedded Systems
- Firmware Engineer
- Radio Frequency (RF) Engineer
- Signal Process Engineer
- Network engineer
- Test Engineer - Semiconductors
- Hardware Validation Engineers
- Research & Development Engineer
- Systems Engineer - IoT
Some specializations may require postgraduate study, hands-on experience or additional technical training
Salary expectation in Irish language
The figures below are broad planning estimates for annual gross salaries not official salary scales or guaranteed offers.
Entry level graduate \| €30,000–€40,000
Early career engineer \| €40,000 - €55,000
Senior Specialist \| €55,000-€75,000+
Actual salaries depend on employer, location, experience, technical specialization and market conditions. Read up on the latest job vacancies and salary surveys for the exact job you want.

faqs.q: Q1. Is there Electronics and Communication Engineering as such ECE in Ireland?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. Similar programs are often offered as Electronic and Computer Engineering or Electrical and Electronic Engineering .

faqs.q: Q2. How long does it take to study an ECE related degree in Ireland?
faqs.a: Many undergraduate honors engineering degrees are four years long. Some integrated Master of Engineering routes are five years, depending on university and course structure .

faqs.q: Q3. What are the tuition fees for foreign students?
faqs.a: Others published for 2026/27 include €17,900 per year at DCU for Electronic and Computer Engineering in Years 1-4 and €27,640 per year at the University of Galway including its listed levy. Additional living expenses and fees are subject to change.

faqs.q: Q4. What are the important subjects for admission?
faqs.a: Mathematics is especially important. Physics and other sciences may be required for undergraduate admission. Masters applicants typically require a related bachelor’s degree and adequate technical preparation.

faqs.q: Q5. What kind of jobs can I find after pursuing ECE in Ireland?
faqs.a: Graduates can find jobs in electronics design, telecommunications, embedded systems, firmware, signal processing, semiconductor testing and network engineering. Career outcomes are based on skills, experience, vacancies and employment eligibility.
